question: Does reserving step 3 for an explicitly indicated keyboard input recover ordinary UI regressions while preserving the first BM25 action?
rule: Use original title and exact historical BM25 and date action menu. Always run ordinary then BM25 top1. If both pass and a named keyboard input appears in the title, reserve the last step for the keyboard action if it is outside the first two BM25 slots. Preserve the complete baseline order in all other cases. No model calls, screenshots, extra reference probe or candidate action budget. Stop at first independently confirmed failure.
known_tradeoff: An explicitly keyboard-related title can also name a relevant second BM25 action. Reserving the last step can displace that action. Log every promotion and displaced action. Distinguish the invariant first pick from observed three-step coverage.
validation: Use frozen public date-picker frame from the earlier six-library inventory and keep the original newest-first round-robin extension ordering. Only inspect closed, ordinary UI issues absent from the enumerated historical experiments. Queue titles with the locked keyboard wording and, in separate strata, those that change or preserve the first three steps. Read upstream reports and repairs in that order as needed. Aim for first qualifying changed-order issue and first qualifying stable-order keyboard issue, permitting issues where BM25 already wins as a negative control. Record skipped docs, unsupported environments, missing release evidence and failed reproductions. The old two-sided text / 5 percent gate belongs to the earlier experiment; record its scores where available and allow keyboard cases outside it in this new protocol.
qualification: Before observing the old release, seal trigger and observable state from the public report, actions, pinned official old and repaired releases, full-menu acceptance and both policy orders. Reference passes every action. Old release passes smoke and unrelated controls; only public signature counts as a regression after repeating in a fresh browser page. Run both policies live in two independent processes on qualifying cases. Fixture changes for a common control are documented with the failed run retained.
scope: Local, public, ordinary date-picker UI and keyboard/accessibility behavior only. No external navigation, security issues, or active production targets.
